dims.label: Type of site
dims.help: Contributor platforms (Mercor, Outlier...), data companies' own job boards, AI labs, big tech.

dims.label: Field
dims.help: The specialist knowledge the job asks for, read from the full listing by a language model (GPT-6.1 Terra). Open a job in the table to see the sentences it used.

dims.label: Kind of task
dims.help: What the work mainly is, read from the full listing by a language model (GPT-6.1 Terra).

dims.label: Language
dims.help: The language other than English the job requires. Jobs asking for two or more are under “Several languages”; the search box finds each language.

dims.label: Degree mentioned
dims.help: Highest degree the listing mentions (mentioned, not necessarily required).

dims.label: Experience asked
dims.help: Smallest number of years of experience the listing asks for.

dims.label: Who can apply
dims.help: Whether the listing limits where you must live or work.
values: Place listed, not said if required

dims.label: Kind of job
dims.help: Contractor unless the listing says otherwise; permanent only when stated.

dims.label: Paid per
dims.help: What the pay figure is for. Salaries are shown per hour at 40 hours a week.

dims.label: How pay is stated
dims.help: One figure (you know the rate), a range (you don't know where in it you will be), or only an "up to" (likely less). A range is a dot at its top, "Range (max)"; tick "Range (min)" to add a dot at its bottom. A few one-figure listings still say the rate depends on something: see "What sets the rate".

dims.label: What sets the rate
dims.help: What the listing says the pay depends on, next to the figure. A range on its own does not say.
values: Amount of work and skill level
Skill level, location and kind of work
